ops.old: لَازِم and يَجِبُ never change: the person is shown on the second verb. لَازِم أَنْ أَرْتَاحَ (I must rest), لَازِم أَنْ تَرْتَاحَ (you must rest), يَجِبُ أَنْ يَنَامَ (he must sleep). لَازِم is very common when people speak; يَجِبُ is a little more formal and common in writing.
ops.new: يَجِبُ never changes: the person is shown on the second verb. يَجِبُ أَنْ أَرْتَاحَ (I must rest), يَجِبُ أَنْ تَرْتَاحَ (you must rest), يَجِبُ أَنْ يَنَامَ (he must sleep). Two other written forms: مِنَ اللَّازِمِ أَنْ (it is necessary that) and عَلَيْكَ أَنْ (you have to, literally 'it is on you'): عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَرْتَاحَ (you have to rest). لَازِم أَنْ is very common when people speak (لَازِم أَنْ أَرْتَاحَ), but it is spoken style: in writing use يَجِبُ أَنْ.
